rule YARA_CobaltStrike_Generic_Fixed {
    meta:
        description = "Detects Cobalt Strike beacons with reduced false positives"
        author = "SOC Team"
        confidence = "high"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        false_positives = ["Packed .NET applications", "Legitimate update binaries"]
        remediation = "Whitelist known-good hashes via threat intel feed"

    strings:
        $beacon_config = { 2E 72 63 64 00 } // ".rcd" string in config
        $http_get = "GET / HTTP/1.1" wide
        $https_beacon = "https://" wide
        $mutex = "Global\\MSCTF.Asm.{" wide

    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and // PE header
        filesize < 500KB and
        all of them and
        not hash.sha256() in ("a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2")
}

arguments.summary: A critical APT intrusion was detected originating from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), attributed to APT-41 (Double Dragon). The attack began with a phishing email triggering an encoded PowerShell execution from Outlook, leading to the deployment of a ShadowPad variant via rundll32.exe. The malware established C2 communication over HTTPS to a known malicious IP (198.51.100.23) and exhibited lateral movement via SMB. Despite detection, initial firewall isolation attempts were misdirected due to IP confusion (10.0.5.14 vs 10.0.5.42), causing a delay in containment. Full EDR scan post-quarantine found no threats, indicating possible in-memory execution or cleanup. Attribution and IOCs confirm TTPs aligned with APT-41, including use of 'Global\APT41_ShadowPad_2026' mutex and C2 domains matching '*.ns[0-9].ezdns.cc' pattern.

        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"

        $b = "windows/beacon" wide ascii

        $http_get = "GET" wide
        $http_post = "POST" wide
    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5a4d and any of ($a, $b) and $c and 2 of ($http_get, $http_post)

arguments.summary: Post-exploitation activity detected originating from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.14). A malicious PowerShell execution chain initiated from Outlook led to the deployment of a Cobalt Strike beacon via an unsigned DLL loaded through rundll32.exe. The payload established C2 communication with a known-bad IP (198.51.100.23:443), attempted lateral movement via SMB, and modified host files. The sandbox analysis initially underestimated the threat due to limited telemetry, but SIEM and EDR data confirmed extensive post-compromise behaviors including credential access attempts and persistence mechanisms. Containment actions included blocking C2 traffic, revoking user CORP\jsmith's credentials, and executing automated remediation to remove malicious artifacts.
